requirements.text: Every vehicle conforming to a vehicle type approved under this Regulation shall have an international approval mark affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form.
The approval mark on the vehicle shall include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.
The approval mark on the vehicle shall include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.1.4.1.

If the vehicle conforms to a vehicle type approved under one or more other Regulations in the country which has granted approval under this Regulation, the circle symbol of paragraph 4.1.4.1. need not be repeated; in such a case the additional numbers and symbols of all the Regulations under which approval has been granted in that country shall be placed in vertical columns to the right of the symbol prescribed in paragraph 4.1.4.1.
The approval mark on the vehicle shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark on the vehicle shall be placed close to or on the vehicle data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

Every separate technical unit (luggage rack, ski rack or radio receiving or transmitting aerial) conforming to a type approved under this Regulation shall have an international approval mark affixed, conspicuously and in a readily accessible place specified on the approval form.
The approval mark on the separate technical unit shall include a circle surrounding the letter "E" followed by the distinguishing number of the country which has granted approval.

The approval mark on the separate technical unit shall include the number of this Regulation, followed by the letter "R", a dash and the approval number, to the right of the circle prescribed in paragraph 4.2.4.1.
The approval mark on the separate technical unit shall be clearly legible and indelible.
The approval mark on the separate technical unit shall be placed close to or on the separate technical unit data plate affixed by the manufacturer.

The provisions of this Regulation shall not apply to those parts of the external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and with all doors, windows and access lids etc. in the closed position, are at a height of more than 2 metres.

The provisions of this Regulation shall not apply to those parts of the external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and with all doors, windows and access lids etc. in the closed position, are below the floor line.

The provisions of this Regulation shall not apply to those parts of the external surface which, with the vehicle in the laden condition and with all doors, windows and access lids etc. in the closed position, are so located that, in their static condition as well as when in operation, they cannot be contacted by a sphere 100 mm in diameter.

The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any pointed or sharp parts or any projections of such shape, dimensions, direction or hardness as to be likely to increase the risk or seriousness of bodily injury to a person hit by the external surface or brushing against it in the event of a collision.
The external surface of vehicles shall not exhibit, directed outwards, any part likely to catch on pedestrians, cyclists or motor cyclists.

No protruding part of the external surface shall have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; this does not apply to parts protruding less than 5 mm, but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.

Protruding parts of the external surface made of a material of hardness not exceeding 60 Shore A may have a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm; the hardness shall be measured with the component as installed on the vehicle, and where a Shore A measurement is impossible, comparable measurements shall be used for evaluation.
The provisions of paragraphs 5.1. to 5.5. shall apply in addition to the particular specifications of paragraph 6., except where these particular specifications expressly provide otherwise.

requirements.text: The junction of the front with the side faces of each element forming a grille or gap shall be blunted.
The wiper shaft of windscreen wipers, rear window wipers and headlamp wipers shall be furnished with a protective casing which has a radius of curvature meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.4.
The protective casing of the wiper shaft of windscreen wipers, rear window wipers and headlamp wipers shall have an end surface area of not less than 150 mm².
The wiper holder (holder head and main holder) of windscreen wipers, rear window wipers and headlamp wipers shall be designed with a radius of curvature meeting the requirements of paragraph 5.4.

In the case of rounded covers on windscreen wipers, rear window wipers and headlamp wipers, these shall have a minimum projected area of 150 mm² when measured not more than 6.5 mm from the point projecting furthest.

Paragraph 5.4. shall not apply to wiper blades, supporting members, second holder, the functional hinge between holder head and holder, or the junction between main and second holder (if present); however, these units shall be so made as to have no sharp angles or pointed or cutting parts.
Compliance of wipers with paragraphs 6.4.1. and 6.4.2. shall be verified with the wipers in parked position.

requirements.text: The ends of the bumpers shall be turned in towards the external surface in order to minimize the risk of fouling; this is considered satisfied if the bumper is recessed or integrated within the bodywork, or the end of the bumper is turned in so that it is not contactable by a 100 mm sphere and the gap between the bumper end and the surrounding bodywork does not exceed 20 mm.

If the line of the bumper corresponding to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 5 mm at all its points lying from the contour line to 20 mm inward, in the part of that zone situated between and in front (or rear for the rear bumper) of the tangential points with the contour line of two vertical planes each forming an angle of 15° with the longitudinal plane of symmetry of the vehicle.

If the line of the bumper corresponding to the outline contour of the car vertical projection is on a rigid surface, that surface shall have a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm in all cases other than the 5 mm zone defined in paragraph 6.5.2.

The requirement of paragraph 6.5.2. shall not apply to parts on or of the bumper or to bumper insets which have a projection of less than 5 mm (in particular joint covers and jets for headlamp washers), but the outward facing angles of such parts shall be blunted, save where such parts protrude less than 1.5 mm.
The requirement of paragraph 6.5.2. does not apply to the bumper cover; the provisions of paragraph 5. remain applicable to the bumper cover.

requirements.text: The projection of handles, hinges and push-buttons of doors, luggage compartments and bonnets and of fuel tank filler caps and covers shall not exceed 40 mm in the case of door or luggage compartment handles and 30 mm in all other cases.
In the case of lateral door handles which rotate parallel to the plane of the door to operate, the open end of the handles must be directed towards the rear.
In the case of lateral door handles which rotate parallel to the plane of the door to operate, the end of such handles shall be turned back towards the plane of the door.
In the case of lateral door handles which rotate parallel to the plane of the door to operate, the end of such handles shall be fitted into a protective surround or be recessed.
Lateral door handles which pivot outwards in any direction not parallel to the plane of the door shall, when in the closed position, be enclosed in a protective surround or be recessed.

The open end of lateral door handles which pivot outwards in any direction not parallel to the plane of the door shall face either rearwards or downwards; handles not complying with this may be accepted if (a) they have an independent return mechanism, (b) should the return mechanism fail, they cannot project more than 15 mm, (c) they comply in the opened position with paragraph 5.4., and (d) their end surface area, measured not more than 6.5 mm from the point projecting furthest, is not less than 150 mm².
The requirements of paragraph 5.4. shall not apply to wheels, wheel nuts, hub caps and wheel discs.
The wheels, wheel nuts, hub caps and wheel discs shall not exhibit any pointed or sharp projections that extend beyond the external plane of the wheel rim.
Wing nuts shall not be allowed on wheels.

When the vehicle is travelling in a straight line, no part of the wheels other than the tyres situated above the horizontal plane passing through their axis of rotation shall project beyond the vertical projection, in a horizontal plane, of the external surface or structure; however, if functional requirements so warrant, wheel discs covering wheel and hub nuts may project beyond it provided the radius of curvature of the surface of the projecting part is not less than 30 mm and the projection in no case exceeds 30 mm.

Sheet-metal edges, such as gutter edges and the rails of sliding doors, shall not be permitted unless they are folded back (by approximately 180°, or towards the bodywork so that they cannot be contacted by a sphere of 100 mm diameter) or are fitted with a shield meeting the requirements of this Regulation applicable to it.

The requirements of paragraph 5.4. shall not apply to the rear edge of the bonnet (including its extrapolation to the left and right, e.g. upper edge of the fender or edge of the A-pillar, limited laterally by the outermost lateral point of the windscreen glass) and to the front edge of the rear luggage boot.

Folds in body panels may have a radius of curvature of less than 2.5 mm provided that it is not less than one-tenth of the height "H" of the projection, measured in accordance with paragraph 1. of Annex 3.
Lateral air or rain deflectors shall have a radius of curvature of at least 1 mm on edges capable of being directed outwards.

The jacking brackets and exhaust pipe(s) shall not project more than 10 mm beyond the vertical projection of the floor line lying vertically above them; as an exception, an exhaust pipe may project more than 10 mm provided it terminates in rounded edges with a minimum radius of curvature of 2.5 mm.
Air intake and outlet flaps shall meet the requirements of paragraphs 5.2., 5.3. and 5.4. in all positions of use.
Opening roofs shall be considered only in the closed position.
Convertible vehicles shall be examined with the hood in both the raised and lowered positions.
For convertible vehicles with the hood lowered, no examination shall be made of the vehicle inside an imaginary surface formed by the hood when in the raised position.
Where a cover for the linkage of the hood when folded is provided as standard equipment on a convertible vehicle, the examination shall be made with the cover in position.
For windows which move outwards from the external surface of the vehicle, in all positions of use no exposed edge shall face forwards.
For windows which move outwards from the external surface of the vehicle, in all positions of use no part of the window shall project beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle.

Supporting brackets provided by the vehicle manufacturer for registration plates shall comply with paragraph 5.4. if they are contactable by a 100 mm diameter sphere when a registration plate is fitted in accordance with the vehicle manufacturer's recommendation.
Luggage racks and ski racks shall be so attached to the vehicle that positive locking exists in at least one direction.

Luggage racks and ski racks shall be so attached to the vehicle that horizontal, longitudinal and transverse forces can be transmitted which are at least equal to the vertical load-bearing capacity of the rack as specified by its manufacturer, tested with the rack fixed to the vehicle according to the manufacturer's instructions and the test loads not applied at one point only.

Surfaces which, after installation of a luggage rack or ski rack, can be contacted by a sphere of 165 mm diameter shall not have parts with a radius of curvature less than 2.5 mm, unless the provisions of paragraph 6.3. can be applied.

requirements.text: Radio receiving and transmitting aerials shall be fitted to the vehicle such that, if their unattached end is less than 2 m from the road surface in any position of use specified by the aerial manufacturer, the unattached end is inside the zone bounded by the vertical planes 10 cm inside the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.

Aerials shall be so fitted to the vehicle, and if necessary their unattached ends so restricted, that no part of the aerials protrudes beyond the extreme outer edge of the vehicle as defined in paragraph 2.7.
Shafts of aerials may have radii of curvature of less than 2.5 mm; however, the unattached ends shall be fitted with fixed cappings whose radii of curvature are not less than 2.5 mm.
The bases of aerials shall not project more than 40 mm when determined according to the procedure of paragraph 2. of Annex 3.

Where, due to the absence of a flexible shaft or part, the base of an aerial cannot be identified, the requirement of paragraph 6.17.4. is deemed to be met if, after a horizontal force of not more than 50 daN in forward and rearward direction is applied by a flat-ended ram of not more than 50 mm diameter at the most salient part of the aerial, (a) the aerial bends towards the support and does not project more than 40 mm, or (b) the aerial breaks off and the remaining part does not show any sharp or dangerous part that can be contacted by the 100 mm sphere and does not project more than 40 mm.

Paragraphs 6.17.4. and 6.17.4.1. shall not apply to aerials located behind the vertical transversal plane passing through the "R" point of the driver, provided that the maximum projection of the aerial including its housing does not exceed 70 mm when determined according to paragraph 2. of Annex 3.

If an aerial is located behind the vertical transversal plane passing through the driver's "R" point but projects more than 70 mm, paragraph 6.17.4.1. shall apply using a projection limit of 70 mm instead of 40 mm.
Luggage racks, ski racks and radio receiving or transmitting aerials approved as separate technical units may not be offered for sale, sold or purchased unless accompanied by assembly instructions.

requirements.text: The height H of a projection of folds in body panels shall be determined graphically by reference to the circumference of a 165 mm diameter circle internally tangential to the external outline of the external surface at the section to be checked, H being the maximum distance, measured along a straight line passing through the centre of the 165 mm circle, between the circumference of that circle and the external contour of the projection (Fig. 1).

Where it is not possible for a 100 mm diameter circle to contact externally part of the external outline of the external surface at the section under consideration, the surface outline in that area is assumed to be that formed by the circumference of the 100 mm diameter circle between its tangent points with the external outline (Fig. 2) when determining the height of a projection.

The dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a convex external surface may be determined either directly or by reference to a drawing of an appropriate section of the component in its installed condition.

If the dimension of the projection of a component mounted on a surface other than convex cannot be determined by simple measurement, it shall be determined as the maximum variation of the distance of the centre of a 100 mm diameter sphere from the nominal line of the panel when the sphere is moved over and is in constant contact with that component (Figure 3).
The projection of headlamp visors and rims from the external surface of the headlamp shall be measured horizontally from the point of contact of a 100 mm diameter sphere (Figure 4).

The dimension of a gap or space between elements of a grille shall be determined as the distance between two planes passing through the points of contact of the sphere and perpendicular to the line joining those points of contact (Figures 5 and 6).
